requirement: Every slave-side accepted request (o_scyc&o_sstb&!i_sstall pre-edge) targets the slave decoded from its address ((a&0xf0)==0x00 -> slave0, 0x10 -> slave1).

Each forwarded request equals the oldest unforwarded mapped request of exactly one master in WE, address, SEL, and write data on SEL-enabled byte lanes (masked lanes are not compared; same rule for stalled-request hold); no request is forwarded twice or invented.
Master ACK/ERR retire that master's oldest outstanding request; ACK only after the corresponding slave ACK; slave ERR maps to ERR.
source: WB B4 3.1.3.2; README 'ACK responses won't get crossed'

requirement: Read data on master ACK equals data the slave returned with its ACK for the same transaction.
Requests to unmapped addresses are never forwarded and must be answered with ERR, not ACK.
Master CYC drop or synchronous reset discards outstanding work; later slave responses to discarded work must not reach masters as completions.
After a reset edge, o_scyc and o_sstb are inactive.
DUT holds stalled slave requests, never STB without CYC, never ACK with ERR on a master port.

A master ERR on a mapped request without a matching slave ERR is recorded as an unresolved obligation (unexplained_mapped_err) with acceptance/ERR cycles; it is never scoped_pass nor credited as a timeout/starvation mechanism. The obligation persists across later reset/restart in the same batch. Decode ERR and matched slave ERR remain handled.
assumptions: Prose insufficient for an exact timeout/arbitration bound; no timer is modeled

requirement: Outstanding obligations at trace end are reported as pending, not as failures.

Declared exclusions: master ACK/ERR while master CYC is low are not attributed (WB B4 3.1.2); post-reset o_mack/o_merr, minimum reset duration, eventual o_scyc withdrawal after abort/timeout, and timeout/starvation latency are not checked.
